chunks: And that which was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man performing Tamattu' who pronounces the Talbiyah for Hajj, then performs Tawaf and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah before his departure to Mina. He said, 'There is no harm with it.'

So it is not invalid for what we mentioned, because this narration came as a concession (rukhsah) for the one we mentioned earlier, namely the elderly Sheikh, the sick person, and the woman who fears menstruation, and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.رُخْصَةً: A concession or dispensation in Islamic law
key_terms.وَيَسْعَى: And performs Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Tawaf and Sa'i before going to Mina for Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms that performing Tawaf and Sa'i before departing for Mina does not break the state of Ihram for a Mutamatti', serving as a specific concession (rukhsah). This ruling is particularly significant for the elderly, the sick, and women fearing menstruation, allowing them to complete these rites early without invalidating their Hajj, thereby facilitating ease in ritual performance.
